summary: Sh. Ali Mashhour continues his discussion on the pillars of Iman (faith) by focusing on belief in the Last Day. He explains that all humans will die and face judgment after death. Sh. Ali Mashhour describes the events of the Day of Judgment in detail: the angel Israfil will blow the horn twice—once to end all life and once to resurrect everyone. He elaborates on the weighing of deeds on scales, crossing the Sirat (bridge over Hellfire), retribution among people, and the final destination of either Paradise or Hellfire. Sh. Ali Mashhour emphasizes that the Day of Judgment lasts 50,000 years, though righteous people will experience it as brief and easy, while wicked people will find it extremely lengthy and difficult. He concludes by stressing that each person is the author of their own book of deeds and can choose their eternal destination through their actions.
